headline: Approved a modified 6-year tax exemption for PurposeEnergy and up to $2 million in TIF funds for 10 Navigator Road.
summary: Approved two ordinances adding alternate members to the Cemetery Trustees, and appointed Gary Della Grotta to the Conservation Commission. Also extended the DPW Facilities Working Group until April 2028 and scheduled hearings for September 21, 2026 and October 5, 2026. Residents raised concerns about legal fees and the Town Manager job description.
decisions: Appointed Gary Della Grotta as a full member of the Conservation Commission, 5-0.
Approved Ordinance 2026-11 adding the Cemetery Trustees to the municipal code, 5-0.
Approved Ordinance 2026-12 describing the charge of the Cemetery Trustees, 5-0.
Approved a modified 6-year commercial/industrial tax exemption schedule for PurposeEnergy, starting April 2028, 3-2.
Approved Resolution 2026-16 on the PurposeEnergy tax exemption, starting April 2028 for 6 years, contingent on final documentation and signing, 3-2.
Authorized the Town Manager to finalize a covenant agreement for a residential food waste drop-off container on PurposeEnergy property, to be presented to Council for final review.
Extended the DPW Facilities Working Group charge until April 2028 and its formal report deadline to April 2027, 5-0.
Scheduled a public hearing for October 5, 2026 on Ordinance 2026-15 updating Town Charter references, 5-0.
Scheduled a public hearing for September 21, 2026 on zoning sections 9.1 and 9.2, 5-0.
Approved Resolution 2026-17 amending the Pettengill Road Tax Increment Finance District, 5-0.
Authorized the Town Manager to enter into an MOU with the Londonderry Housing and Redevelopment Authority on TIF funds for 10 Navigator Road, 5-0.
Approved the consent items, the August 17, 2026 Council minutes and the August 17 LUCT bills, 5-0.

Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves a modified 6-year Commercial/Industrial Tax Exemption schedule beginning April 2028 (50% Year 1, 45% Year 2, 36% Year 3, 25% Year 4, 15% Year 5, 8% Year 6). plain_text:
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — September 14, 2026 
Page 1 
Londonderry Town Council Meeting Minutes 
Monday, September 14, 2026 | 7:00 p.m. 
Moose Hill Council Chambers, Londonderry Town Hall 
Council Members Present: 
Chair Ron Dunn 
Vice Chair Shawn Faber 
Councilor Dan Bouchard 
Councilor Deb Paul 
Councilor Ted Combes 
Council Members Absent: 
None 
 
Meeting Link: 
http://173.166.17.35/internetchannel/show/14328?c
hannel=4 
Other Staff Present: 
Town Manager Shaun Mulholland 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen 
Minutes Prepared By: 
Kirsten Hildonen using Gemini Notebook AI 
 
A. CALL TO ORDER 
Chair Dunn called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and led the Pledge of Allegiance. 
Councilor Combes requested a moment of silence in memory of Marilyn Webster Ham, who 
recently passed away at the age of 97. Mrs. Ham was a long-time Londonderry resident who 
founded the Londonderry Heritage/Historic District, was appointed Town Historian in 2005, and 
served with her husband Chet as Grand Marshals of the 2007 Old Home Day parade. 
Chair Dunn shared a letter of appreciation from Battalion Chief Bruce Howell highlighting 
Londonderry Fire Rescue members. On the evening of May 19th, department members 
voluntarily repaired and rebuilt a damaged roadside memorial cross and stone at Old Nashua 
Road and Parmenter Road dedicated to a local teenager lost in a past crash, demonstrating 
exceptional care and respect for the community. 
B. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment. 
Name: David Ellis 
Address: 1 Wilshire Drive 
Mr. Ellis read a statement regarding two proposed job description documents for the Town 
Manager position. He emphasized that the standard job description requires managing a 
$50M+ budget and 200+ employees with clear separation of executive and legislative 
responsibilities under the Town Charter, whereas Councilor Dunn's draft contained ambiguous 
language. Chair Dunn informed Mr. Ellis that the item had been removed from the evening's 
agenda. 
Name: Glenn Douglas 
Address: 6 Overlook Drive
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — September 14, 2026 
Page 2 
Mr. Douglas inquired about waiving attorney-client privilege regarding the Veterans Tax 
Credit legal opinion, noting Councilor Bouchard agreed to sponsor the item for a future agenda. 
He expressed concern over legal fees of $500/hour and delays in fulfilling 91-A requests 
concerning documents read on August 17. 
Name: Linda Lampkin 
Address: 4 Griffin Road 
Ms. Lampkin spoke against Council micromanagement of the Town Manager, drawing parallels 
to previous library trustee actions that led to high legal fees and lost personnel. She urged the 
Council to allow the Town Manager to perform his administrative duties. 
Name: Richard Bielinski 
Address: 89 Hall Road 
Mr. Bielinski reported that the salvage yard business at 55 Hall Road was sold in August and is 
operating under new ownership without a personal license or governing body approval, in 
violation of RSA 236:114 and court orders regarding property signage and equipment display. 
Name: Pedro Florez 
Address: 4 Cimmaron Drive 
Mr. Florez expressed concern regarding property damage to his lawn caused by an ongoing 
road construction project near his home. Chair Dunn and Town Manager Mulholland directed 
Mr. Florez to meet with Administrative Services Director Hildonen in the hallway to seek a 
resolution to the matter. 
Name: Paul Skudlarek 
Address: 20 Woodbine Drive 
Mr. Sklar addressed three topics: (1) Urged postponing adoption of the Town Manager job 
description until after the March 2027 election; (2) Submitted an addendum for the citizen 
petition letters approved in April (Article 27 and Article 28) requesting signatures from 
remaining Councilors; (3) Announced his candidacy for State Representative. 
Name: Martha Smith 
Address: 38 Shasta Drive 
Ms. Smith expressed full support for Mr. Skudlarek’s remarks regarding citizen petition letters, 
stating that articles passed with strong voter backing should be forwarded to Concord with 
complete Council representation. 
Councilor Paul asked if they could still sign the letters and Chair Dunn affirmed they could. 
Name: Isaac Fernandez 
Address: 10 Walton Circle 
Mr. Fernandez, Budget Committee member, supported Mr. Skudlarek’s statements on 
property taxes and cost downshifting, requested Councilors sign the petition addendum, and 
announced his candidacy for State Representative. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — September 14, 2026 
Page 3 
Councilor Bouchard raised concerns regarding increasing legal expenses, pointing to recent 
billings. He requested that all legal research, opinions, and analysis be shared with all five 
Councilors, noting legal expenditures are tracking near $40,000 per month. 
Vice Chair Faber stated that the $40,000 monthly total includes general Town legal expenses 
unrelated to Council matters, and advised against publicly detailing active legal matters to protect 
attorney-client privilege. 
Councilor Paul reiterated requests for transparency regarding legal opinions, subcommittee 
actions, and the choice of legal counsel. Chair Dunn noted that legal updates were provided during 
the August 31 consultation with legal counsel. 
C. BOARD APPOINTMENTS AND REAPPOINTMENTS 
1. Discuss the appointment of Gary Della Grotta from an alternate to a full member of 
the Conservation Commission. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby appoints Gary Della Grotta as a 
full member of the Conservation Commission. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 5-0-0. 
Chair votes in the affirmative. 
D. PUBLIC HEARING 
1. Receive public input, discuss, and approve adding alternates to the Cemetery 
Trustees. 
Administrative Services Director Hildonen presented Ordinance 2026-11 and Ordinance 2026-
12 pursuant to RSA 289:6 and 7, allowing the Council to appoint up to two one-year alternate 
members to the three-member Cemetery Trustees board to assist with quorums, while updating 
references and municipal code charge descriptions. 
Councilor Combes moved to open the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion 
carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Chair Dunn asked for public comment; there was none. 
Councilor Combes moved to close the public hearing. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 
5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves Ordinance 2026-11 
adding the Cemetery Trustees to the municipal code and correcting outdated lists, references, and 
other errors. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves Ordinance 2026-12 
describing the charge of the Cemetery Trustees. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion carried 
5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — September 14, 2026 
Page 4 
2. Receive public input, discuss and approve the application for a Commercial / 
Industrial Tax Exemption for PurposeEnergy. 
Town Manager Mulholland and representatives Ari Pollock, Esq. and Mark Riley of 
PurposeEnergy presented the application for a commercial/industrial tax exemption under RSA 
72. The presentation detailed job creation (25-30 total positions with partner Recycle Works), 
regulatory permits received, odor mitigation controls, property valuation projections ($2.5M in 
taxes paid over 10 years), and a proposed residential food waste drop-off container. 
Councilor Combes moved to open the public hearing. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 
5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Public Comment: 
• Martha Smith (38 Shasta Drive): Commended her visit to the Vermont facility, questioned job 
numbers and Stonyfield waste participation. 
• Ray Breslin (3 Gary Drive): Questioned trucking volume, out-of-state waste origin, investor 
financing, and requested delaying tax relief decisions. 
Councilor Combes moved to close the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion 
carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
The Council debated exemption terms. Councilors Bouchard and Paul opposed granting tax 
exemptions to commercial entities. Councilors Dunn, Faber, and Combes agreed on a modified 6-
year phase-out schedule. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves a modified 6-year 
Commercial/Industrial Tax Exemption schedule beginning April 2028 (50% Year 1, 45% Year 2, 
36% Year 3, 25% Year 4, 15% Year 5, 8% Year 6). Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 
3-2-0, with Councilors Paul and Bouchard voting in opposition. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves Resolution 2026-16 
regarding the Commercial/Industrial Tax Exemption for PurposeEnergy as stated, beginning April 
2028 for a 6-year period, contingent upon final documentation and signing. Seconded by Councilor 
Combes. Motion carried 3-2-0, with Councilors Paul and Bouchard voting in opposition. Chair votes 
in the affirmative. 
The Council authorized Town Manager Mulholland to finalize the covenant agreement for the 
residential food waste drop-off container on PurposeEnergy property with paved access, to be 
presented to Council for final review. 
Councilor Paul requested scheduling a future discussion to evaluate repealing or sunsetting the 
Commercial/Industrial Tax Exemption ordinance. 
E. NEW BUSINESS 
1. Discuss and approve the extending the charge of the DPW Working Group. 
Administrative Services Director Hildonen reviewed the progress of the DPW Facilities Working 
Group, highlighting outreach events at the past Old Home Day, at the upcoming Senior Expo (Oct
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — September 14, 2026 
Page 5 
3), and upcoming Household Hazardous Waste Day (Nov 21). Hildonen requested extending the 
group’s report deadline to April 2027 and its formal charge through April 2028 to support project 
execution. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby extends the charge of the DPW 
Facilities Working Group until April 2028 and extends the deadline for a formal report to April 
2027. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
2. Discuss and schedule a public hearing for October 5, 2026 to approve updating the 
Charter references. 
Administrative Services Director Hildonen presented Ordinance 2026-15 to update cross-
references throughout the municipal code to align with the revised Town Charter section 
organization. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby schedules a public hearing 
on October 5, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. in the Moose Hill Chambers of the Londonderry Town Hall for 
Ordinance 2026-15 regarding approval of updated references to the Town Charter in the municipal 
code. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
3. Discuss and schedule a public hearing for September 21, 2026 regarding the proposed 
revisions to the Londonderry Zoning Ordinance (LZO) to incorporate the 2024 ICC 
International Building Codes as amended by the State of NH and recent legislative 
changes. 
Administrative Services Director Hildonen explained proposed revisions to sections 9.1 and 9.2 of 
the zoning ordinance adopting the 2024 ICC building codes as mandated by state legislation, 
removing local technical amendments while maintaining administrative permitting processes and 
incorporate recent legislation affecting Building and Code Enforcement activities. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby schedules a public hearing 
for September 21, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. in the Moose Hill Chambers of the Londonderry Town Hall 
regarding proposed revisions to section 9.1 and 9.2 of the Londonderry zoning ordinance. Seconded 
by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
F. OLD BUSINESS 
1. Approve the proposed changes to the Pettengill Road TIF District. 
Following the August 17 public hearing, the Council considered adding four properties to the 
Pettengill Road Tax Increment Finance (TIF) District and approving an MOU with the 
Londonderry Housing and Redevelopment Authority (LHRA) to utilize up to $2 million in TIF funds 
for building improvements at 10 Navigator Road, offset by guaranteed motor vehicle registration 
revenues. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves Resolution 2026-
17 to amend the Pettengill Road Tax Increment Finance District. Seconded by Councilor Combes. 
Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — September 14, 2026 
Page 6 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council authorizes the Town Manager to 
enter into the Memorandum of Understanding with the Londonderry Housing and Redevelopment 
Authority regarding the use of TIF funds for improvements to the property located at 10 Navigator 
Road and to take all actions necessary to effectuate the MOU. Seconded by Councilor Combes. 
Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
G. APPROVAL OF CONSENT ITEMS 
1. Town Council meeting minutes from August 17, 2026 
2. August 17 LUCT bills 
Vice Chair Faber moved to approve the consent items. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion 
carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
H. OTHER BUSINESS 
1. Liaison Reports 
Councilor Bouchard reported on his attendance at the New Hampshire Municipal Association 
(NHMA) legislative policy conference on September 11th, emphasizing the importance of 
protecting municipal local control. Chair Dunn noted the Council voted in March not to send an 
official voting delegate. 
2. Town Manager Report 
Town Manager Mulholland updated the Council on FY2028 budget preparation, stating warrant 
articles will be presented early on October 5. He noted new non-taxpayer revenues offsetting 
associated operational expenses. Upcoming items include the DPW Pavement Condition Index 
(PCI) presentation and FY2026 closeout on Oct 19. Quarterly financial status reports will be made 
available on the Town budget website page.  
I. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment. 
Name: Richard Bielinski 
Address: 89 Hall Road 
Mr. Bielinski raised questions regarding salvage yard enforcement at 55 Hall Road, fire chief 
compensation updates, competitive bidding policies for data collection traffic signs, benefit 
warrant article financial disclosures for the Town Clerk, and transparency regarding $131,000 
in staff salary adjustments. 
Councilor Bouchard spoke in defense of town staff and code enforcement officers, commending 
their diligence and asking that personal attacks on municipal employees cease. 
Councilor Combes requested distributing the petition letter addendum presented by Mr. 
Skudlarek for signatures by remaining Councilors.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — September 14, 2026 
Page 7 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
J. NON-MEETING 
Chair Dunn announced the Council would transition to a non-meeting session following 
adjournment. 
K. ADJOURNMENT 
Vice Chair Faber moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion carried 
5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. The meeting adjourned at 10:02 p.m. 
L. MEETING SCHEDULE 
• September 21, 2026, Moose Hill Council Chambers, 7:00 p.m. 
• October 5, 2026, Moose Hill Council Chambers, 7:00 p.m. 
• October 19, 2026, Moose Hill Council Chambers, 7:00 p.m.
